summary: Vinit Deo works in Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned an external MA in Indology from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (2022–2024) and held an alumni post at Indira Gandhi National Open University in 2024.

Vinod Kumar Roy specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Patna University, Magadh University, and the University of Delhi, where he completed a BA and a PhD (1992–2003), later becoming Assistant Professor at Magadh University in 2019.

Vinod Mishra is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned an MSc from Kurukshetra University (1989–1991) and a PhD from Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (1994–1998), becoming a Professor at Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology in 2010.
Vipul Jadav is an Indologist who completed a PhD in Sanskrit at Shree Somnath Sanskrit University (2017–2021). He was appointed Assistant Professor at the same university in 2020.
Virchand Gandhi (1864–1901) worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Mumbai and Elphinstone College (~1880–1884) and taught Herbert Warren.
Virendra Kumar Varma worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramnath Dixit and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and he taught Kamala Prasad Tripathi.
Virendra Kumar Verma worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under teachers Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopal Chandra Mishra, and he taught Kamala Prasad Mishra.

Virendra Nath Misra (1935–2015) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961), serving as Director of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1990–2000).
Vishal Agarwal is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Vasudha Narayanan. He held an attested post at the Library of Congress in 1999.

Indologist Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar (1887–1943) studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin under Lüders, Jacobi, and Winternitz. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and became General Editor at BORI in 1925.

Vishva Bandhu (1897–1973), an Indologist and linguist, studied under Alfred Cooper Woolner. He served as Founder-Principal of Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921) and long-time Director of the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1934–1973), where he founded the Indological Series.

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1848–1851), served as an examiner at the University of Mumbai, and was Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878).

Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as a Professor at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973–1978 and 1987).

Vishwanath Mishra (1930–2016) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ram Yash Tripathi and Badrinath Shukla, taught at Jain Vishva Bharati Institute, and instructed Ramyatna Shukla and Ashok Kumar Tiwari.

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under teachers Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1942–1944), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, and Joachim Wach (1950), with Kali Kinkar Datta as his doctoral supervisor.

Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam (1925–2002) studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram Universities. His career included serving as Director of the Scindia Oriental Institute (~1972–1985) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1986–1989; 1992–1995) and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1996–1998).

Vitalij Petrovič Furnika (1940–1993) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Semën Gesselevič Rudin in 1965, attended Saint Petersburg State University (1965–1970), and studied at the University of Madras (1969–1970).

Vittore Pisani (1899–1990), a linguist and Indologist, earned his PhD at Sapienza under Formichi and Pagliaro. He held chairs at Florence, Cagliari, Bocconi, and especially Milan (1938–1969), and founded the journal Paideia in 1946.
Vittorio Bettei worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a teacher of Latin and Greek at Liceo Ginnasio Benedetto Cairoli and Liceo Canova.

Vittorio Rocca (1862–1905) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pisa (~1881–1885). He held a post as docent at Sapienza University of Rome and obtained a libera docenza in Sanskrit at Pisa in 1905.
